## Purpose

Fix the PLE (per-layer n-gram embedding) short-conv state handling of `qwen4_exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, so that a request resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD) reads a valid conv state, and so that the blocks the prefix cache and the offloading tiers store for the PLE group are actually written.

Part of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tracking issue #55922 (KV offload section). Same component as #59642 (PD side of the PLE state). Possibly related symptoms: #55357 (episodic 0% MTP acceptance with prefix caching on), #53912.

## Root cause

In align mode the PLE metadata builder (`short_conv_attn.py`) takes `block_table[:, 0]` of the align-gathered block table, i.e. the block of the last *scheduled* token, and uses it both to read the initial conv state and to write the final one. The Mamba/GDN backends instead receive `block_idx_last_computed_token` and read the resumed state from the block of the last *computed* token inside their kernels; the PLE conv kernel has no align support at all.

Two consequences:

1. A request resumed at, say, 6400 computed tokens with 3714 new tokens has its loaded state in block 1 but the PLE reads block 3, which was just allocated and never written. On GB10 TP=2 that memory contained NaN: the NaN appeared in the PLE output of layer 1 with clean inputs, crossed ranks through the TP all-reduce, and MTP acceptance went from ~2.2 to exactly 1.0 (no draft ever accepted) with garbage output. With finite garbage in that memory the state is silently wrong instead.
2. Blocks that end at a 3200-token boundary crossed by a prefill chunk are never written, so the prefix cache and the offloading tiers store uninitialized memory for the PLE group. Inspecting the stored blocks showed NaN in the PLE slot of every block of that group.

GPU-local flows (chunked prefill, local prefix hits) were not affected because the KV cache manager copies the state forward for them; connector loads do not go through that path.

## Changes

- `short_conv_attn.py`: in align mode compute per row the carry source (block holding the state after the computed tokens) and destination (block the kernels address). Decode and spec rows go into persistent builder buffers padded with `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, like `spec_state_indices_tensor`, so full CUDA graph replay reads valid indices. Prefill rows also carry the block-table rows, `seq_lens` and `num_computed_tokens` needed to write boundary checkpoints.
- `ple_layer.py`: copy the conv state from source to destination before each conv (decode, spec and prefill paths); after a prefill, write the exact state at every block boundary the chunk crossed into the block ending there, and zero the speculative scratch columns so stored blocks never carry garbage.

No behavior change when `mamba_cache_mode != "align"`: the new metadata fields stay `None` and the layer code paths are skipped.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU tier + fs tier), `mamba_cache_mode=align`, MTP k=3, prefix caching on, TP=1 on GB10. Load: 48 conversations of ~10.1k tokens (3200 shared system prompt + 6600 per-conversation context), 256 requests at concurrency 4, so most hits come from the offloading tiers (6400-token external hits, ~49% of prompt tokens overall).

## Test Result

Before (same load, TP=2): MTP acceptance correlated 1:1 with external hits, from ~2.2 at 0% hits to 1.0 at 14% hits; NaN born in the PLE of layer 1 on the first resumed prefill; stored PLE blocks contained NaN.

After (TP=1): 256 requests, no NaN in any layer across all 17,751 probe records, MTP acceptance 2.19 average at 49% external hits, stored PLE blocks fully initialized with the scratch columns zeroed.

TP=2 could not be validated on this cluster: the GB10 nodes have one GPU each, and with multi-node TP the tiering manager (CPU tier + fs tier) runs in the scheduler process on rank 0's node and only sees that node's mmap region. Only `_r0` files are ever written, rank 1 never creates the secondary tier, and on a load rank 1 copies a stale slot from its own `/dev/shm`. The result is wrong but finite KV on rank 1 (0 NaN in the layer probe, MTP acceptance collapses to 1.0 as soon as external hits start), independent of this fix. That is the known single-host assumption of #54415, addressed by #46556; it also explains why the NaN in my first TP=2 runs always appeared on rank 1. A TP=2 validation of this fix needs a single host with two GPUs.

Note: the three crashes I hit while developing this were all mine (a missing broadcast, a token-index clamp on the wrong length in mixed spec/non-spec batches, and fresh builder tensors captured by the CUDA graph); the final version went through 256 requests in two separate runs without errors.

@@ -188,6 +188,76 @@ def get_state_shape(self) -> Sequence[tuple[int, ...]]:
             num_spec=self.num_spec_tokens,
         )
 
+    def _ple_carry_state(
+        self,
+        conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+        src: torch.Tensor | None,
+        dst: torch.Tensor | None,
+        ncols: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        """Copy the state from the last computed token's block (src) into the
+        block the kernels address (dst). Rows with src == dst are no-ops."""
+        if src is None or dst is None or dst.numel() == 0:
+            return None
+        sub = conv_state[..., :ncols]
+        sub.index_copy_(0, dst.long(), sub.index_select(0, src.long()))
+        return dst
+
+    def _ple_write_checkpoints(
+        self,
+        conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+        inputs_p: torch.Tensor,
+        token_indices_p: torch.Tensor | None,
+        query_start_loc_p: torch.Tensor,
+        bt_p: torch.Tensor,
+        seq_lens_p: torch.Tensor,
+        num_computed_p: torch.Tensor,
+        bs: int,
+        kmax: int,
+        init_state: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Materialize the exact state at every block boundary a prefill
+        chunk crosses, into the block ending there, and zero its scratch."""
+        sl = self.conv_state_len
+        dev = conv_state.device
+        r = seq_lens_p.numel()
+        k = torch.arange(kmax, device=dev)
+        c0 = num_computed_p[:, None] // bs
+        p = (c0 + 1 + k[None, :]) * bs  # [R, K] boundaries > c
+        valid = p <= seq_lens_p[:, None]
+        off = p - num_computed_p[:, None]  # offset into the chunk, >= 1
+        cols = ((p // bs) - 1).clamp(min=0, max=bt_p.shape[1] - 1)
+        blocks = bt_p.gather(1, cols.long())  # [R, K]
+        j = torch.arange(sl, device=dev)
+        pos = off[..., None] - sl + j  # [R, K, SL], < 0 -> from the initial state
+        qsl = query_start_loc_p[:r].to(dev)
+        # In mixed batches inputs_p is the full tensor and token_indices_p
+        # maps prefill-relative positions into it: clamp on the index space.
+        n_tok = (
+            token_indices_p.numel()
+            if token_indices_p is not None
+            else inputs_p.shape[0]
+        )
+        tok = (qsl[:, None, None] + pos.clamp(min=0)).clamp(max=n_tok - 1)
+        if token_indices_p is not None:
+            tok = token_indices_p[tok]
+        win_in = inputs_p[tok.long()].transpose(2, 3)  # [R, K, C, SL]
+        init_col = (sl + pos).clamp(0, sl - 1)  # [R, K, SL]
+        c = init_state.shape[1]
+        win_init = (
+            init_state[:, None]
+            .expand(r, kmax, c, sl)
+            .gather(3, init_col[:, :, None, :].expand(r, kmax, c, sl).long())
+        )
+        win = torch.where((pos >= 0)[:, :, None, :], win_in, win_init)
+        sel = valid.reshape(-1)
+        blocks_f = blocks.reshape(-1)[sel].long()
+        if blocks_f.numel() == 0:
+            return
+        win_f = win.reshape(r * kmax, c, sl)[sel].to(conv_state.dtype)
+        conv_state[..., :sl].index_copy_(0, blocks_f, win_f)
+        conv_state[..., sl:].index_fill_(0, blocks_f, 0)

+        bs = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size

+        idx = idx.to(device=bt.device, dtype=torch.long)

+            return {}
